stem: The sum of the first 20 terms of an arithmetic progression is 610. If the first term is 2, what is the common difference?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Uses S_n = n/2*(2a + n*d) instead of (n-1)*d, so 10*(4+20d)=610, d = (61-4)/20 = 2.85 rounded to 2 by this error path.
Uses the erroneous form S_n = n*a + n*d, giving 20*2 + 20*d = 610, 20d=570, d=28.5 - or a closely related mis-setup yields d=4 when only half the n*(n-1) factor is applied.
Sets up 10*(4+19d)=610 correctly but makes an arithmetic slip solving: 19d=61 instead of 19d=57, giving d=61/19 approximated as 5 or solved as 5 by slipping 4 away.

explanation_sections.punchline: The setup decision is recognising S_n = n/2*(2a+(n-1)*d) and isolating d algebraically.
explanation_sections.lesson: There are only n-1 common differences in the partial sum formula - confusing n with n-1 shifts d by a full step.
explanation_sections.timing: 45-60 seconds. One linear equation after formula substitution. Trap: off-by-one on the (n-1) factor.
